themes.note: Every token is declared three times in site/index.html: bare :root (light), @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded as :root:not([data-theme="light"]), and :root[data-theme="dark"]. Frontmatter carries the light values; the dark value of each token is recorded as colorMeta.<token>.dark.

grain.purpose: Opacity of the fixed pulp.png tile behind the page; the dark sheet takes more grain, as a press proof would.

stock.purpose: The sheet. Page ground and input ground, overlaid by the fixed grain tile.

stock-2.purpose: Half-tone deeper sheet: order stub, coupon perforation, kbd keys, scrollbar track.

ink.purpose: All headings, prose and hard strokes (1px stub/input/coupon, 2px section underlines).

ink-2.purpose: Secondary prose: colophon, step explanations, option descriptions, rail heads.

ink-3.purpose: Faintest set ink: unticked tick-box stroke, plate captions, scrollbar thumb.

cyan.purpose: Links, recognised-platform marks in the order queue. Brightens in dark so link ink stays legible on dark stock.

cyan-field.purpose: Whole-region ground for disclosure blocks and ::selection. Identical to cyan in light; deepens in dark so near-white text on the field keeps contrast.

verm.purpose: Stamp ink only: step numerals, refusal crosses, focus ring, caret, hover ink, confirmed-copy field.

plate.purpose: The catalog photograph: command plates, plate captions, source listing. Does not invert with the theme.

plate-tx.purpose: Near-white command text on the plate. Same value in both themes.

plate-rl.purpose: 1px divider between a plate caption bar and its plate.

btn-face.purpose: Printed label stock for copy buttons; stays light in both themes.

btn-face2.purpose: Darker label stock for the secondary button beside a primary.

rule.purpose: Heavy separating rule: 3px entry openers and 4px full-bleed bars. Tracks the ink, so it inverts with the theme.

hair.purpose: 26%-opacity ink hair dividing rows, rails and dotted contents leaders.

display.purpose: The name, once per sheet. Chivo 900 caps at display scale.

title.purpose: Masthead strap at 26ch, step headings, ruled pull statements at 40ch.

lede.purpose: One honest sentence under every entry heading, max 44ch.

label.purpose: Plate captions, coupon field labels, rail heads, all button text. 11-13px, .1em to .16em.

mono.purpose: Colophon, rail copy, queue rows, landing line, inputs and select.

plate.purpose: Command plate text; the source listing drops to 12px / 1.62.

motion.name: strike
motion.value: strike 90ms steps(2, end); from scale(1.2) rotate(-16deg) to rotate(-7deg)
motion.purpose: The only animation in the build. Lands the tick stamp inside its box. Declared only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

motion.name: copy-confirm
motion.purpose: A copied button holds the vermilion field with white text, then reverts. An instant swap, not a fade.

breakpoints.name: sheet
breakpoints.purpose: Max width of .sheet; full-bleed rules sit outside it.

breakpoints.name: fold
breakpoints.purpose: The only breakpoint. Below it the masthead and entries collapse to one column, the stub hides, and plates wrap with a hanging indent.

rasters.use: Fixed body::before ground tile at opacity var(--grain); also the coupon inner ground.
rasters.provenance: PNG tEXt impeccable:prompt, procedurally generated by .impeccable/assets/mkassets.py

rasters.use: 45-degree dot screen tiled on every .plate, .plate-head and .listing.
rasters.provenance: PNG tEXt impeccable:prompt, procedurally generated by .impeccable/assets/mkassets.py

rasters.use: Inked check impression revealed inside every ticked box, resting at rotate(-7deg) and overhanging its box.
rasters.provenance: PNG tEXt impeccable:prompt, procedurally generated by .impeccable/assets/mkassets.py

components.name: Stamp Button
components.description: The printed label that copies a command. Takes the vermilion field for 1600ms once it has copied.
components.html: <button class="ds-stamp" type="button">Copy</button> <button class="ds-stamp ds-stamp-quiet" type="button">Show raw yt-dlp</button> <button class="ds-stamp" type="button" data-done="1">Copied</button>
components.css: .ds-stamp { font-family: 'Chivo', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .1em; white-space: nowrap; background: var(--btn-face, #cfcdc2); color: #15150e; border: 0; border-radius: 0; padding: 6px 13px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-stamp-quiet { background: var(--btn-face2, #a3a196); } .ds-stamp:hover { background: #fff; } .ds-stamp[data-done="1"] { background: var(--verm, #b8371c); color: #fff; } .ds-stamp:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-stamp:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--verm, #b8371c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Command Plate
components.description: A dark halftone-screened plate holding a command, with a caption bar and copy button above it. Each real line is its own span so the mobile hanging indent applies per line.
components.html:
Paste into Terminal
pipx install "yt-dlp[default,curl-cffi]"pipx ensurepath
components.css: .ds-plate-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px 12px; flex-wrap: wrap; background-color: var(--plate, #16160f); background-image: url(assets/halftone.png); color: var(--ink-3, #6d6d5e); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--plate-rl, #34342a); padding: 8px 15px; font-family: 'Chivo', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .14em; } .ds-plate { background-color: var(--plate, #16160f); background-image: url(assets/halftone.png); color: var(--plate-tx, #e4e1d3); font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7; padding: 14px 15px; overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre; border-radius: 0; } .ds-ln { display: block; } .ds-plate-btn { font-family: 'Chivo', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .1em; background: var(--btn-face, #cfcdc2); color: #15150e; border: 0; padding: 6px 13px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-plate-btn:hover { background: #fff; } @media (max-width: 860px) { .ds-plate { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-ln { padding-left: 1.3em; text-indent: -1.3em; } }

components.name: Tick Row
components.description: The coupon's option control and the system's state model: a bare aria-pressed button whose ticked state is an inked stamp landing crooked in the box, never a fill or a hue.
components.css: .ds-modes { display: grid; } .ds-mode { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 26px minmax(0,1fr) auto; gap: 12px; align-items: baseline; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: none; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--hair, rgba(21,21,14,.26)); padding: 11px 0; font: inherit; color: var(--ink-2, #4f4f42); cursor: pointer; } .ds-mode:last-child { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hair, rgba(21,21,14,.26)); } .ds-tick { width: 18px; height: 18px; border: 1.5px solid var(--ink-3, #6d6d5e); position: relative; align-self: start; margin-top: 2px; display: block; } .ds-tick img { position: absolute; left: -7px; top: -9px; width: 31px; height: 31px; display: none; transform: rotate(-7deg); } .ds-nm { font-family: 'Chivo', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: -.008em; display: block; } .ds-ds { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.45; display: block; margin-top: 2px; max-width: 54ch; } .ds-sp { font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 11.5px; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--ink-2, #4f4f42); } .ds-mode[aria-pressed="true"] { color: var(--ink, #15150e); } .ds-mode[aria-pressed="true"] .ds-tick { border-color: var(--ink, #15150e); } .ds-mode[aria-pressed="true"] .ds-tick img { display: block; } .ds-mode:hover .ds-nm { color: var(--verm, #b8371c); } .ds-mode:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--verm, #b8371c); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-tick img { animation: ds-strike 90ms steps(2, end); } } @keyframes ds-strike { from { transform: scale(1.2) rotate(-16deg); } to { transform: scale(1) rotate(-7deg); } }

components.name: Cyan Field Block
components.description: A whole region flooded with the process cyan, reserved for the statements the page most needs believed. The system's substitute for a card.
components.html:
This page cannot touch your computer

Every button here copies text to your clipboard. You paste it into Terminal yourself.
components.css: .ds-field { background: var(--cyan-field, #0b6a89); color: #eef6f9; padding: 22px 24px; margin: 20px 0; border-radius: 0; } .ds-field h3 { font-family: 'Chivo', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #fff; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 900; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .04em; margin: 0 0 8px; } .ds-field p { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; font-size: 16.5px; line-height: 1.62; color: #e4f0f5; max-width: 62ch; margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Stock ground, hard ink stroke, typewriter text, vermilion caret. Used for the link textarea and the masthead stub input.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; display: block; background: var(--stock, #d3d1c6); color: var(--ink, #15150e); border: 1px solid var(--ink, #15150e); border-radius: 0; padding: 11px 12px; font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7; resize: vertical; min-height: 84px; caret-color: var(--verm, #b8371c); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-2, #4f4f42); opacity: 1; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--verm, #b8371c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Warning Block
components.description: A hard vermilion-ruled box for the one thing that reliably frightens people (the blind password prompt). Border only; vermilion stays a mark.
components.html: It will ask for your Mac login password. Nothing appears while you type. The screen is not frozen.
components.css: .ds-warn { border: 2px solid var(--verm, #b8371c); border-radius: 0; padding: 11px 13px; font-family: 'Chivo', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.45; max-width: 58ch; color: var(--ink, #15150e); }

components.name: Margin Rail Contents

narrative.overview:
Snag is a cheap-offset mail-order tool catalog printed between 1968 and 1974, reproduced exactly. The ground is pulp stock, grey-olive and deliberately not cream, carried by a real 256x256 procedural grain tile fixed behind the page rather than a flat fill. Ink is heavy near-black. One process cyan carries whole regions of the sheet, not accents. A cheap vermilion is held back for stamps and marks only. Commands are set in dark halftone plates the way a catalog sets its photographs, and those plates stay dark in both themes because a photograph does not invert with the paper.

Density is catalog density: every entry is its own two-column sheet with a marginal access rail, and the rails, rules and stamps do all the separating. There is no card system, no border-radius anywhere in the build, and no box-shadow anywhere in the build. Depth is ink weight and full-field colour, nothing else. Dark theme is not a second world; it is the same sheet as a press proof, with ink and stock swapped and the grain pushed harder.

The page's authority is its honesty, and the visual system serves that: the honest paragraph is Source Serif, the machine is Courier Prime, and the imperative is Chivo 900 caps. Confirmed rejection: the centred dark terminal hero with a one-line install box and a copy button. This sheet does not centre, does not put a hero image anywhere, and prints the whole script on the page before it asks anyone to run anything.
keyCharacteristics: Pulp stock ground with a real grain tile at token-controlled opacity (0.55 light, 0.9 dark)
One process cyan as a field, one vermilion as a mark, nothing else chromatic
Dark halftone command plates that never invert with the theme
Rules and hairlines instead of cards; zero radius, zero shadow
Three fixed voices: Chivo display and UI, Source Serif 4 prose, Courier Prime machine
Stamped motion only: one 90ms step animation, dropped entirely under reduced motion

rules.name: The Colour-Is-The-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Cyan arrives as a field, not a mark. When cyan appears, it owns a whole block edge to edge with its own light text; it is never a tint, a badge, or a 1px accent border.

rules.name: The Vermilion-Is-A-Mark Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is only ever a stamp, a numeral, a cross, a caret, a focus ring, or a hover ink. The single exception in the build is the 1600ms confirmed-copy state on a stamp button, which is itself a stamp landing. Never a section ground, never body text.

rules.name: The Plate Does Not Invert Rule
rules.body: The stock and the ink swap between themes. The plate, its halftone screen and its text do not. A command plate is a photograph on the sheet, and it reads the same in light and in dark.

rules.name: The Split-Token Rule
rules.body: Where one token cannot hold both themes at legible contrast, split it by job, not by tint: cyan is ink, cyan-field is ground. Read the split as a contrast mechanism, not as a two-step ramp.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Chivo speaks for the catalog (names, headings, labels, buttons). Source Serif 4 speaks the honest evaluation. Courier Prime speaks for the machine and the margin. A voice never takes another's job; prose is never set in mono for texture, and a command is never set in the serif.

rules.name: The One Imperative Per Sheet Rule
rules.body: Display scale is spent once, on the masthead. Every other heading steps down to headline or below, so the sheet has exactly one thing shouting.

rules.name: The Printed-Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from ink weight, grain and field colour. If a surface needs to feel separate, give it a rule, a field or a plate. Never a shadow, never a glow, never a lift on hover.

rules.name: The No-Card Rule
rules.body: There is no card. Separation is a rule, a hairline, a stamp or a full-field colour. Nothing gets a rounded corner, a lifted edge or a container chrome it did not earn as print.

rules.name: The Stamped-Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion lands, it does not travel. Every animated state change is a stepped impression of 90ms or less, and under reduced motion the system drops to no movement at all rather than to a shortened tween.

rules.name: The Every-Option-Present Rule
rules.body: All choices are printed at once, with the chosen one struck forward by the stamp. Nothing collapses into a dropdown to hide what the visitor is turning down, except the native resolution cap, which is a numeric range rather than a set of choices.

dos: Do paint cyan as a whole field with its own light text, not as an accent or a tint.
Do keep vermilion for marks: numerals, crosses, carets, focus rings, hover ink and stamps.
Do set every command in a dark halftone plate, one <span class="ln"> per real line, with the exact text on dataset.raw for copying.
Do separate with rules, hairlines, stamps and full-field colour; use a 3px rule to open an entry and a full-bleed 4px rule to close a region.
Do put .fullrule outside .sheet so rules reach the viewport edge while type stays in the 1160px column.
Do keep .bodycol before .marg in the DOM and restore the visual left rail with CSS order.
Do hold the three voices apart: Chivo for names, headings, labels and buttons; Source Serif 4 for evaluation prose; Courier Prime for commands and marginalia.
Do show state as an inked impression at rotate(-7deg), not as a fill or a hue change.
Do cap measure: 44ch for a lede, 68ch for prose, 62ch inside a cyan field, 40ch for a pull statement.
Do theme the browser surfaces (::selection, focus ring, scrollbar, caret) so the sheet does not stop at the content edge.
donts: Don't add a border-radius. The build has none, anywhere, in any state.
Don't add a box-shadow, a glow, or a hover lift. Depth is ink weight, grain and field colour.
Don't introduce a card, a panel or a tile. Rules and plates do the separating.
Don't invert the command plate with the theme. The plate is a photograph, and it stays dark on light and on dark stock.
Don't let a fourth colour in. The system is stock, ink, one cyan, one vermilion.
Don't animate anything longer than 90ms or with an eased tween; steps(2, end) is the grammar, and reduced motion means no movement.
Don't spend display scale twice on one sheet.
Don't clip a command. Below 860px plates wrap with a 1.3em hanging indent per line.
Don't put a hero image, a centred terminal block, or a single install box with a copy button at the top of a sheet. That is the category default this world refuses.
